The Wexley Family Foundation supports registered Canadian charities improving girls' attendance and learning in Southern and East Africa. Priority areas: safe water, toilets and menstrual-health facilities in primary and secondary schools. Grants of $40,000 to $90,000 for 12-24 months. Applications are accepted on a rolling basis through a short online form (8 questions, budget template). Decisions within eight weeks. Annual reporting.

The Community Vitality Fund invests in projects that strengthen health, environment and belonging for people who live in the Maplehurst Region. This round prioritizes clean water and climate resilience. Grants up to $40,000. Deadline: November 28, 2026. Eligible applicants: registered charities and qualified donees. All funded activities must directly benefit Maplehurst Region residents.

Elmsworth Foundation funds registered charities working on water security and climate adaptation anywhere in the world. Grants range from $40,000 to $120,000. The application deadline is September 30. Applicants are notified in January. [Page footer: Last updated May 2025]
Halvard employees can nominate a registered charity they care about for a Giving Grant of $2,500 to $10,000. Nominations are open year-round. Charities cannot apply directly.
Ashgrove Foundation (Toronto). Focus: health, water. Grant range $25,000-$150,000. Letters of inquiry accepted twice yearly. Source: 2019 annual report.
column11: The Ashgrove Family Foundation accepts two-page letters of inquiry on February 15 and September 15 each year. We fund registered charities in global health, water and girls' education, with a preference for Africa. Invited proposals follow within six weeks.

column8: We support registered charities working in international development and global health. To keep our grants meaningful, applicants must have total annual revenue below $2 million in their most recent fiscal year. Grants of $20,000 to $100,000. Applications due January 20, 2027.

Cindermoor provides rapid funding within 30 days of a declared humanitarian emergency to organizations with active emergency operations on the ground. Current open window: Cyclone response, Mozambique (declared October 2, 2026). Water, sanitation and shelter. Up to $200,000.

column4: (no call page) - Global Health Systems envelope
column8: ...In 2026 the Board approved a new five-year Global Health Systems envelope of $3 million per year, focused on primary health care in sub-Saharan Africa. Recognizing that clinics cannot deliver safe care without water, sanitation and infection prevention, the envelope will consider multi-year grants of $150,000 to $600,000 to registered Canadian charities. Letters of inquiry will be accepted between November 1 and December 12, 2026...
column11: Our current grant programs: Canadian Arts Access; Ontario Youth Mental Health. (No mention of Global Health Systems.)

column8: Linden & Crane funds registered charities advancing health equity internationally. Grants $75,000-$200,000 for one year. Indirect/administrative costs may not exceed 5% of the request. Deadline: December 5, 2026. Annual reporting.

Kestrel Bay supports Indigenous-led organizations in Canada and around the world protecting water and land. Applicants must be Indigenous-led (majority Indigenous board and leadership). Grants of $25,000-$200,000. Deadline February 13, 2027.

The Resilient Futures Fund supports registered charities reducing climate and disaster risk for vulnerable communities worldwide. Grants of $100,000 to $300,000 over two years. Applications close December 1, 2026.
column11: Rivermark Insurance Group today launched the 2027 Resilient Futures Fund... Charities are invited to apply by November 15, 2026. (Press release dated September 22, 2026.)

column8: Thornbury funds registered charities advancing gender equality and health globally. Our open call typically opens in spring, with grants of $50,000-$150,000. Sign up for our newsletter to be notified.
Corvane Foundation (Vancouver). Climate adaptation, global. Grants $100,000-$750,000. Annual call, spring. Listing last verified June 2025.
column11: March 4, 2026: Corvane's new CEO announces that, beginning with the 2027 call, the Foundation will focus exclusively on climate adaptation in Canadian communities. Existing international grants will be honoured to completion.

column8: La Fondation Quillon soutient les organismes de bienfaisance enregistrés ayant un bureau au Québec, pour des projets en santé des femmes et des filles en Afrique francophone et en Haïti. Les demandes doivent être déposées en français avant le 20 novembre 2026. Subventions de 50 000 $ à 250 000 $.

Tessaly invests in maternal and newborn health systems in sub-Saharan Africa and South Asia, including water, sanitation and infection prevention in birthing facilities. We do not accept unsolicited proposals; our Board invites organizations in March and September. Grants of $200,000 to $1 million over three years.

Brenmoor invests in water, health and education within 50 km of our operations in Alberta, the Copperbelt (Zambia) and Tete Province (Mozambique). Partnerships of $25,000-$300,000, reviewed on a rolling basis, with quarterly reporting.

column3: Northlight Pooled Fund for Grassroots Water
column8: Northlight funds community-based organizations registered in sub-Saharan Africa to lead their own water projects. International NGOs and their country affiliates are not eligible. Grants of $10,000-$60,000. Deadline December 10, 2026.

We fund women-led organizations advancing women's leadership worldwide. A women-led organization has a woman in its most senior staff role and a board on which women hold leadership positions. Grants $30,000-$120,000. Deadline January 9, 2027.

Canadian organizations with prior federal international assistance experience may apply for $1M-$5M over four years for climate adaptation and water security in eligible countries. Gender equality must be a principal objective. Full proposals, logic model, risk register and budget due November 9, 2026. 10% cost-share required.
Harrowgate supports registered charities delivering water and sanitation in Africa. Current geographic focus: Ghana, Senegal and Sierra Leone. Grants $50,000-$250,000. Deadline December 15, 2026.

Pellworth makes grants to US 501(c)(3) public charities and to foreign organizations that hold a current equivalency determination. Focus: water, sanitation and health worldwide. Grants $50,000-$300,000. Deadline January 31, 2027.
Larkspur Trust funds registered charities improving water and health outcomes globally. Grants $100,000-$350,000. Deadline December 1, 2026.
column11: The Trust's endowment includes a continuing holding in Larkspur Tobacco Holdings Inc., the founding family's company.

column8: Harold Venn-Moraes (major donor, Dunmore trustee's cousin): 'The trustees are open to hearing from Water Care again next year, but they remember the late report. A conversation before any ask would help.'

Granville Tide funds registered charities building climate-resilient water security in sub-Saharan Africa and South Asia, with priority for gender-responsive approaches and district-level systems. Grants $150,000-$450,000 over three years. Full proposals due January 22, 2027. Semi-annual reporting.

Sorrel Ridge funds water infrastructure across Africa. Grants $250,000-$500,000. Every grant requires a 1:1 cash match from the applicant or co-funders, confirmed at submission. Deadline January 15, 2027.
